topic: Various checks on propeller on the ground during ground run
syllabus_extract: Various checks on propeller on the ground during ground run
specific_objectives: 7.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to explain propellers and its associated maintenance practice

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Conduct ground run checks on propeller; Safety: Ensure clear area and proper RPM limits; Supervision: Instructor monitors all readings and safety protocols
intro_questions: What is the primary purpose of a ground run check?
List three safety precautions before starting a ground run.
Which instruments are typically monitored during a propeller ground run?

development.content:
Pre-run safety inspections
Engine start and idle verification
RPM gauge reading and stability
Vibration and noise assessment
Blade tracking visual check

Thrust bearing temperature monitoring
Oil pressure and temperature checks
Fuel flow and mixture settings
Electrical system load testing
Cooling system efficiency verification

Post-run shutdown procedures
Final visual inspection for damage
Documentation of run data
Comparison with standard limits
Reporting anomalies to maintenance

summary_questions: Explain the significance of monitoring thrust bearing temperature during a ground run.
Describe the correct procedure for documenting ground run data for maintenance records.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report outlining the key differences between ground run checks and in-flight propeller inspections, referencing LP 02.
